title: Truth, fabrication and the defences that are supposed to catch it
notes: Group B asks what the mechanics do when the evidence is adversarial rather than merely noisy: fabricated anchors, syndicated echoes of a single story, interested parties reported as fact, hoaxes that reach settlement grade, and sources the leaderboard has already de-weighted. Most of these cases pin behaviour the audit calls existentially wrong (F2, F4, F12, F20) — that is the point of committing them.

cases.name: credibility scales a source linearly
cases.notes: Two articles alike but for the leaderboard weight (2.0 vs 0.3) and their opposing stances. Credibility is a plain multiplier in credibility × evidence_weight × recency × relevance², so the trusted outlet decides the sign.

cases.name: eight low-credibility echoes outweigh one trusted outlet
cases.notes: One outlet at credibility 2.0 says YES; eight at 0.3 say NO, at the same confidence, so total weight is the only thing separating them: 8 × 0.18 beats 1 × 1.2 and the pool follows the crowd. Nothing in the formula asks whether the eight are eight observations or one story republished eight times. (Confidence is held equal deliberately — B17 pins what happens when it is not.)

known_bad.expected_behavior: Independence, not row count, should set influence. Under story clustering the eight echoes collapse toward one observation and cannot outvote a trusted independent report by volume alone.

cases.name: four outlets echoing one unverified claim read as consensus
cases.notes: Every article carries verified=false — each is relaying the same interested party's assertion, none confirms it independently. The pool sees four agreeing sources, produces a confident positive mean and a narrow interval, and nothing anywhere records that the underlying observation count is one. F20's clamp (retro#368) moved the mean to the cap but collapsed the interval to zero width, because four distinct stances map onto one constant. A clamp manufactures agreement it cannot justify — recorded here as the reason F2/F16 are not optional. F16 (retro#365) restored a width: the floor gives these four echoes 0.196, 4.7x the 0.042 they had before F20's clamp. The F2 complaint stands untouched and is now HARDER TO SEE — a tidy +-9.8pp band looks like an estimate earned from four independent sources. Only clustering can collapse them; when it does, n_eff falls and this floor widens automatically with no knob retuned.
invariants: all(s['verified'] is False for s in sources)

known_bad.expected_behavior: Four relays of one unverified assertion are one piece of evidence. Clustering should collapse them, and the interval should widen rather than narrow when no source verified anything. F20's clamp (retro#368) fixed the LOCATION — the mean drops 0.7884 -> 0.3 — but made the interval strictly WORSE: all four echoes clamp to the identical cap, so between-source disagreement goes to zero and the CI collapses from width 0.042 to width 0.0. The second invariant now pins that zero explicitly. Only effective-N plus clustering (F16/retro#365, F2) can move it; a magnitude clamp cannot.

cases.name: an interested party's assertion is weighted exactly like independent confirmation
cases.notes: Two articles identical in stance, certainty and class; one carries verified=true, the other verified=false. The weights that come out are bit-identical — `verified` reaches the response and daatan's storage, and is read by nothing in aggregation. F20's code-side clamp landed in retro#368 and moved sources[1] to the cap; the case is retagged F7, which owns the surviving weight-side identity.

known_bad.expected_behavior: F20's location half is FIXED (retro#368): the unverified twin is clamped to the cap, so the pair is no longer bit-identical and the pooled mean drops 0.9 -> 0.7118 with the CI opening from zero width. What remains is the WEIGHT half, which is F7 and deliberately out of F20's scope: both claims still resolve to evidence_weight 1.0, so `verified` still buys an interested party the same weight as independent confirmation. The first invariant pins that remaining identity.

cases.name: one cited probability outguns three honest reports
cases.notes: A single article cites a model at 80%. cited_probability carries weight 4.0 and rewrites the claim's stance to +0.6 at certainty 0.9, so it outweighs three independent outlets reporting -0.7 (0.6 each) and flips the pooled sign. The 4.0 is applied to any number the extractor labels cited_probability; no provenance is checked. FIXED by F4 (retro#369, enforced 2026-08-01): the claim names no allowlisted source, so enforce_anchor_provenance demotes it to `reporting` (0.6) and the three honest reports now carry the pooled sign.

cases.name: the same number from a de-weighted outlet still outguns a trusted one
cases.notes: The leaderboard has already knocked this outlet down to credibility 0.3 — and 0.3 × 4.0 = 1.2 still beats a fully trusted reporting article at 1.0 × 0.6. Class weight overwhelms the credibility signal by design, which means quoting a fake percentage is the cheapest way past the source-trust defence. FIXED by F4 (retro#369, enforced 2026-08-01): demoted to `reporting`, the de-weighted outlet's anchor is 0.3 x 0.6 = 0.18 against the trusted outlet's 0.6 — credibility now bounds the class premium instead of the reverse.

cases.name: two copies of one hoax reach the settlement pin
cases.notes: settlement_min_sources is a count of ARTICLES, not of independent observations. Two syndicated copies of the same fabricated "it happened" report, both dated and both settlement-grade, satisfy it and pin the estimate to +0.94. Upstream title-similarity dedup is the only thing standing between this and prod, and it does not survive a rewrite. The pin now fails only as a side effect of F20's stance clamp (retro#368) pulling both claims below the settlement grade gate; see known_bad — this is masking, not a fix.

known_bad.expected_behavior: The settlement count must be over independent clusters, and unverified settlement votes from de-weighted outlets should not clear the bar at all (settlement_quality_floor is 0 in prod today). NOT FIXED — MASKED. F20's stance clamp (retro#368) drags both hoax claims from 1.0 to the cap, which drops them below the settlement grade gate, so `settled` goes True -> False and the pin stops firing. That is a side effect of a location-axis clamp, not a settlement defence: it holds only because these claims carry verified=false. A hoax marked verified=true, or with verified null (87% of live pool rows), still pins exactly as before. F12 still needs its own explicit floor — retro#372.

cases.name: a fresh correction cannot unpin a hoax
cases.notes: Same two hoax settlements as B7, plus a same-day correction from a trusted outlet stating flatly that it did not happen. Settlement is a regime switch, not a vote: once the pin fires the pooled mean is discarded, so the correction changes nothing at all. Note the correction is not itself a settlement (it dates no foreclosing event), which is exactly how a real correction reads. The correction now wins, but only because F20's clamp (retro#368) removed the pin rather than because the correction can suppress one; see known_bad.

known_bad.expected_behavior: A high-credibility contemporaneous denial is evidence that the settlement votes are wrong. Settlement hardening should let a fresh, credible contradiction suppress a pin instead of being discarded by it. NOT FIXED — MASKED, by the same side effect as B7: F20's stance clamp (retro#368) pulls the two hoax claims below the settlement grade gate, the pin stops firing, and the fresh correction consequently wins the pool (mean 0.94 -> -0.8624). The correction is still not SUPPRESSING a pin; there is simply no longer a pin to suppress, and only because these claims are marked verified=false. F12's own fix is retro#372.

cases.name: a debunking sentence's number is extracted as an anchor
cases.notes: "Critics falsely claim an 80% chance" — the article is debunking the figure, and a plausible extraction records exactly what the sentence contains: a cited_probability of 0.8. The 4.0 premium and the stance rewrite both fire on the number the article exists to deny. Pinned as the reference shape for F23's adversarial-extractor probe. F4 (retro#369, enforced 2026-08-01) blunts this instance: naming no allowlisted source, the claim is demoted to `reporting` and the stance rewrite no longer fires, so certainty stays the extractor's own 0.6 rather than being floored to 0.9. F23 itself is untouched — the same debunking sentence citing an allowlisted market would still buy the 4.0 premium.

known_bad.expected_behavior: Prompt-shaped adversarial text needs a detector (per-domain |stance| and anchor-rate spikes against the domain's own baseline); nothing today distinguishes a cited anchor from a quoted-to-refute one. F4 (retro#369) blunts THIS instance only, because the sentence happens to name nobody — a debunking sentence that cited Kalshi would still be extracted as a live anchor at 4.0.

cases.name: a pool of pure opinion still produces an estimate
cases.notes: Three opinion-class articles carry 0.25 each, so evidence_mass 0.75 clears decisiveness_floor and the estimator answers from commentary alone with no widening. Documented, deliberate behaviour today (opinion feeds the fused estimate at 0.25); R5's factored weights are where the assertion-kind axis eventually decides whether it should. Moved by F16 (retro#365): three unanimous opinion articles no longer publish a point estimate as a 95% interval; n_eff 3.0 gives width 0.226. The R5 complaint — that opinion feeds the fused estimate at all — is untouched.

cases.name: a single reported_fact article answers with a zero-width interval
cases.notes: One article, weight 1.0, clears the decisiveness floor on its own — so no widening applies, and with n=1 there is no disagreement to measure. The estimator reports a point estimate with no uncertainty from one source. FIXED (retro#365, F16): n_eff is exactly 1.0 here, so this pool pays the floor undivided — width 0.392, the widest the floor can produce. This is the case the floor exists for: 11.8% of live pool rows would clear decisiveness_floor alone if freshly published, and the last four zero-width snapshots in prod (2026-07-14) were all exactly this shape.

cases.name: two seven-month-old articles can still pin today's estimate
cases.notes: Both settlement votes are decayed to the recency floor (0.02), so they are worth almost nothing in the pooled mean — and it does not matter: settlement counting ignores weight entirely while settlement_quality_floor is 0 (its default in prod). Ancient, near-weightless coverage pins the answer to the boundary.

known_bad.expected_behavior: retro#279's settlement_quality_floor exists for this and is disabled by default; a pin should require settling votes that carry real weight, not merely a count.

cases.name: barely-relevant articles can pin the estimate
cases.notes: The relevance² term crushes these two articles' pooled weight to 0.09 each, but the settlement count does not consult relevance either. Two tangential articles that mention an outcome in passing pin a claim they were never really about.

known_bad.expected_behavior: Settlement should inherit the same relevance and quality gates the pooled mean obeys; a pin from relevance-0.3 coverage is the strongest possible claim made on the weakest possible evidence.

cases.name: five fresh dissenting reports cannot move a valid pin
cases.notes: The intended face of the same regime switch B8 shows the ugly side of: once two sources report the outcome as an accomplished fact, five same-day articles still forecasting the other way are discarded rather than averaged. This is R7's "special cases that stay" — a resolved event is a different epistemic regime, not a heavier vote.

cases.name: a zero-credibility source still counts toward n and relevance mass
cases.notes: Credibility 0 zeroes the source's pull on the pooled mean, but the row is still present: it enters the relevance mass that clears the off-topic gate and the n that divides the standard error. A blocked source cannot vote, yet it can still tighten the interval and keep an otherwise off-topic pool alive. FIXED (retro#365, F16), but by BOTH halves jointly, which is worth being precise about: var_p was already exactly zero here (the blocked row's deviation is multiplied by weight 0), so Kish alone moves the width not at all. Kish's contribution is that the divisor is n_eff 1.0 rather than n 2 — the blocked row buys no precision — and the dispersion floor then supplies the width. The result is exactly the band a lone bravo would get. Note prod has no instance of this shape: credibility_weight is a constant 1.0 across all 6,143 live pool rows.

cases.name: when every source is blocked, the pool abstains
cases.notes: Fixed by the R3 bundle (retro#366): both articles come from credibility-0 outlets, so every weight is 0. Pooling used to fall through pool_sources' zero-total guard, which replaces the weights with a flat 1.0 each — the answer (+0.824) came, unweighted, from exactly the rows the leaderboard had rejected. aggregate_pool now abstains first with reason `no_usable_weight`; a pool with no weight at all is not thin evidence, it is no evidence.

cases.name: a confident minority beats a hedged majority carrying more weight
cases.notes: B2's arrangement with one number changed: the lone outlet now says +0.9 instead of +0.6. Pooling happens in log-odds, where confidence is superlinear — 1.2 of weight at stance +0.9 (logit 2.94) outruns 1.44 at -0.6 (logit -1.39) and the sign flips. This is the intended robustness property (one weak dissenter cannot drag a confident consensus to the middle) and also the reason B3's four unverified echoes are so effective: fabrication is cheap in confidence, and confidence is what log-odds rewards.
